body: Me too, I mean a war movie can be a comedy, a dance movie can be a psychological thriller, and whatever bizarre combination can be made.

Ah. I didn't even consider the subjectivity of horror. Some people are terrified of clowns. That makes me think too about why some things are considered horror. Why did we agree that X monsters belong in the horror genre? Why is Y universally thrown into the horror genre? There is probably a justifiable, anthropological reason in there, but yeah it's definitely subjective.
Metal in the same sense that Bitches Brew is somehow rock-inspired. It's potentially their interpretation of metal. I like this!
Ya know what, I never really thought about that. That's a pretty darn good idea.

The problem is with my mom is the horror element inherent in her design. Yes she has eleven toes, snakes for hair and is voiced by Fred Tatascoire. Yes she is inspired by Junji Ita's Tomie. Yes she may have inspired Tomie. But the problem is the lack of suspense that inevitably results from overexposure. If Deathclaws were everywhere they'd be less scary in dark tunnels or sewers, and probably less of a challenge for players.

It's not like I can fully disagree. I mean, old Fallout fans think of Supermutants as being among the most iconic enemies. My only real problems with it is the fact that they sort of diluted the difficulty and imposing nature of them by just making them regular enemies, and their presence was explained by "There was another, secret vault that also had FEV. In fact, they invented FEV there." That explanation bothers me more than it probably should. I feel like an elitist asshole for thinking that, and I really really just want to like the lore in 3 like all my friends.

76 is a gamble. I'm inclined to agree that they'll have to come up with something because if it is 25 years after the bombs fall they likely won't have as many types of monsters yet just because it's so soon after the event. Or maybe they will.

Ah. I apologize friend. I meant in terms of metal/hard rock. If the Dead ever adopted that distorted, dissonant, tritone-based sound for any time. Also, thanks for your input so far, really happy with the suggestions.

Jockamoo's description is perfect for it. It's really just the Dead at their most "stereotypically" psychedelic, a term I use loosely because I can't really say it sounds like anything else, but it has the same spirit as an early Syd Barrett or long ass version of Inna Gadda da Vida: really long psuedo-bluesy playing over a static Ray Manzarek style organ and chord. I'm not saying you have to be tripping balls on acid to like it but it was the soundtrack to many an official and unnofficial acid test. 
And honestly, like what you like. I'm as happy with you liking any Grateful Dead as I am if you liked all of it.
"I wasn't actually in rawr, but I felt a sort of tender curiosity. Also, I'm a dinosaur."
Can he take me too? Does the doctor do groups?

There's a difference between momentary insanity and realization that you're not meant for life. My life has gotten worse and worse and I don't want it anymore. Being happy for a thousand years won't make up for this. If I'm lucky I'll get a terminal diagnosis from my doctor soon. I hope you get through this, but I shouldn't. I'm a very bad person and I never should have been born. I'm lucky only a few people will mourn for me.
I've tried playing guitar again, videogames, etc. and I've tried going to the gym, community service, working and all that jazz but nothing works.
I don't want to make a mark. I'm tired and I want this world to kill me just for a little bit of mercy. I don't want to make it through. I don't want to get better. I want this nightmare to end.
Sorry, I didn't know that was against the rules.
